messages.subject: occuMulti and condensing detections
parts:
Hi there,

I am new to occuMulti but am familiar with occu and colext. For occu and colext you can condense your detections into for example 3, 4 or 5 day periods. When doing this in order to test which condensed period is the best, you test your global occupancy model for each period and species for goodness-of-fit, which ever period has the best fit, is the one you use for analyses. This condensing is especially valuable for rare species. Therefore, I was wondering whether there was a similar method that could be used to determine what the best condensing period would be for multiple species being used in occuMulti? 

Thank you in advance,
Jess

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: occuMulti and condensing detections
parts:
Hi Jess,

I think you could use the same general approach you describe with occuMulti. However with occu and colext you have more ways available to check fit - e.g. you can use the mb.gof.test function from package AICcmodavg with occu/colext, but this is not available for occuMulti. Thus you would be limited to less specialized fit tests like the ones in the parboot example.

If it were me, I'd probably be less focused on fit and more on choosing period length in order to get a reasonably high probability of detection. It would also be a good idea to test multiple periods and make sure they all give reasonably similar results. Perhaps others who have dealt with this choice can chime in.

Ken
